# Conformance cases excluded from the automatic CI and nightly matrix.
#
# Every other case in testdata/ runs on every push to main and every night.
# A case listed here does not - it is run on demand, by naming it in the
# debug-conformance workflow, which takes explicit case names and ignores this
# file.
#
# This exists so a resource that cannot be covered for free still gets covered.
# Without it the choice is between no conformance case at all and adding
# recurring spend to every run, and the first option is how types end up
# shipping broken - a fifth of this plugin's types had no case, and writing the
# first one for a type found a real defect almost every time.
#
# List a case here only for a reason that survives being written down: it costs
# real money to hold, it mutates something shared, or the API cannot be made to
# accept it at all. Slowness alone is not a reason; that is what the per-case
# timeouts are for. Neither is "it is failing" - a failing case is a bug to fix,
# and the only admissible version of that reason is a demonstrated, written-down
# refusal on the provider's side.
#
# One case name per line. Blank lines and # comments are ignored.

# A PRODUCTION Bigtable instance with two clusters bills per node per hour, and
# a DEVELOPMENT instance - which the other Bigtable cases use - cannot have a
# second cluster at all, so there is no cheap way to exercise this type.
bigtable-cluster

# analyticshub queryTemplates.create cannot be satisfied by a service account,
# and a service account is the only identity CI has (github-deploy@, via
# workload identity).
#
# The API checks primaryContact twice, format first and identity second, and
# demands it equal the authenticated caller's own email. Probed 2026-09-03
# against development-477117: a malformed value answers "The QueryTemplate
# primary contact should be either a valid email or URL"; a well-formed address
# belonging to somebody else answers "Primary contact must be the same as the
# authenticated user's email". Sent by a human caller, the CI service account's
# own address clears the format check and fails only the identity one - so the
# string is well-formed. Sent by that service account as its own contact, it
# fails the FORMAE check instead, which is only consistent if the complaint is
# about the caller's resolved email. A service account does not have one, so no
# value satisfies both checks.
#
# The type itself works: created, patched and deleted by hand under a human
# identity on the same date, which is what the fixture, the createOnly flags on
# displayName/primaryContact/documentation and the update transformer were
# written against. To run this case, use a user identity - locally, with
# "gcloud auth application-default login" and FORMAE_TEST_CALLER_EMAIL set to
# that account. Naming it in debug-conformance will not help; that runs as the
# same service account.
analyticshub-query-template
